name: Al-Ruhban
body:
AL-Ruhban
CR 2

This tall humanoid has light silvery-gold hair and pale skin covered with odd tattoo-like symbols and patterns in sky-blue pigment that match the color of its eyes. Its arms are unusually long, with its hands dangling to its knees.

XP 600
N Medium humanoid (air)
Init +3; Senses darkvision 60 ft.; Perception +4

DEFENSE

AC 15, touch 13, flat-footed 12 (+2 armor, +3 Dex)
hp 19 (3d8+6)
Fort +3, Ref +6, Will +2
Resist electricity 5, sonic 5

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft.
Melee mwk scimitar +5 (1d6+2/18–20)
Special Attacks spellstrike
Space 5 ft.; Reach 10 ft.
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 3rd; concentration +4, +8 to cast defensively)

3/day—shocking grasp
1/day—gust of wind (DC 13), invisibility

STATISTICS

Str 14, Dex 17, Con 14, Int 13, Wis 12, Cha 13
Base Atk +2; CMB +4; CMD 17
Feats Combat Casting, Combat Reflexes
Skills Knowledge (arcana) +4, Perception +4, Stealth +6
Languages Auran, Common Gear leather armor, mwk scimitar

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Spellstrike (Su)

Whenever an al-ruhban casts a spell with a range of touch, it can deliver the spell through any weapon it is wielding as part of a melee attack. Instead of the free melee touch attack normally allowed to deliver the spell, the al-ruhban can make one free melee attack with its weapon (at its highest base attack bonus) as part of the casting of this spell. If successful, this melee attack deals its normal damage as well as the effects of the spell. This attack uses the weapon’s critical range, but the spell effect only deals x2 damage on a successful critical hit.

ABOUT

The al-ruhban are the offspring of a djinni and a humanoid.

An al-ruhban typically appears as the same race as their humanoid parent, though they tend to be taller than average and often have some physical characteristic that hints at their extraplanar bloodline, such as an odd hair or eye color.

The commanding aura of their sky-blue eyes and noble stance hint at something else.

Some al-ruhban remain in the courts of their djinni kin, though most djinn view them as low in station due to what they see as a diluted bloodline. Many more seek a living among their humanoid kin. Most keep a low profile, hiding their lineage and passing themselves off as nothing more than another member of whatever race they are descended from. Some few flaunt their differences, considering themselves exceptional, and thus due admiration, respect, and whatever riches they can acquire. This wealth can be consequential, as the al-ruhban can live for centuries, with an average lifespan of 500 years.

The main reason for the secrecy of the al-ruhban is that certain ambitious wizards and other powerful folk believe they can use the genie-kin for their own ends. Some seek to harvest the powers of the elements from them through experimentation. Others wish to use them as bargaining chips, holding the al-ruhban hostage to leverage their djinn parent into acquiescing to the kidnapper’s demands.

Those that flaunt their lineage seek to leverage their power, putting themselves into a position of fame and/or power that leaves them untouchable by those that would seek to use the al-rhuban in their machinations and power-grabs.
